key_insight: The paper shows that coding-agent performance is strongly shaped by specific harness components—not just the model itself. By fixing the execution loop and varying planning, action space, and context management separately, the study makes it possible to see which harness design choices actually improve long-horizon coding outcomes.
problem_solved: Existing evaluations treat coding harnesses as one black box, making it hard to tell which parts of the system help or hurt autonomous coding agents. This paper addresses the lack of component-level understanding in harness design for software-engineering benchmarks.
method: Build a lightweight coding harness with a fixed execution loop.
Systematically vary three components: planning, action space, and context management.
Compare component effects across four different models to isolate which design choices matter most.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work provides a clearer basis for designing and evaluating coding-agent systems. It helps teams choose harness components more intentionally, improving reproducibility and potentially boosting real-world agent performance.
visual_elements: A modular harness diagram showing the fixed loop and the three variable components.
A comparison matrix or heatmap of performance across planning, action space, and context management.
A flowchart illustrating how a coding task moves through the agent harness.
Icons for each component: plan, tools/actions, and memory/context.
paper_title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
paper_authors: Run-Ze Fan, Zihao Zhang, Simin Ma, Yebowen Hu, Shouju Wang
